source.title: LLM Surgery: Efficient Knowledge Unlearning and Editing in Large Language Models
source.authors: A. Veldanda; Shi-Xiong Zhang; Anirban Das; Supriyo Chakraborty; Stephen Rawls; Sambit Sahu; M. Naphade

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. The Table 1 text layout is flattened, but the main LLM Surgery values are also stated in the prose.
record.tranche_reason: The paper applies a combined gradient-ascent unlearning method and evaluates targeted-knowledge accuracy, but it does not test the recovery attacks in the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates unlearning and retention after LLM Surgery and its ablations. It does not apply fine-tuning recovery attacks, activation-direction ablation, quantization, or prompting attacks. Its activation-pattern analysis does not test whether an activation edit restores knowledge or whether access is blocked rather than knowledge deleted.
record.test_reason: The paper proposes a gradient-ascent-based unlearning method (LLM Surgery) and reports targeted-knowledge accuracy and retained general ability on Llama2-7B. That bears on the first half of version A. It applies no recovery attack: no fine-tuning, activation edits, quantization or prompting, so versions B–F are untested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The authors conclude that LLM Surgery achieves significant forgetting on the unlearn set, a 20% gain on the update set and maintained retain performance, with 35x fewer GPU hours than retraining. They also conclude that all three objective terms are needed.
record.recipe_differences: Uses gradient ascent on the unlearn dataset, combined with gradient descent on an update dataset and KL-divergence minimization on a retain dataset.
record.method_sensitivity: The ablation results indicate that omitting gradient ascent prevents effective unlearning, while omitting KL-divergence is associated with reduced retain-set performance.

fits_no_version.finding: After LLM Surgery, activation patterns differ on unlearn and update data but stay similar to θpre on retain data (Figure 1, qualitative).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient-ascent unlearning shifts activation patterns on targeted data while preserving them on retain data.

record.problems: Only Llama2-7B is tested. No uncertainty estimates are reported. The paper does not state a chance-level value. Table 1 is flattened for the ablation results, so some values cannot be assigned reliably. No recovery attacks are tested.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results relevant to the tested claim versions were left out. Update-set accuracy and runtime comparisons were omitted because they do not measure the claim's targeted-knowledge recovery or retention outcomes.

untested.parts: Whether simple attacks (relearning, prompting, quantization, activation edits) recover the unlearned knowledge.
Not tested: no relearning fine-tuning after unlearning.
Not tested. The activation-pattern figure is descriptive and includes no ablation or blocked-versus-deleted test.
Not tested: no rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context probes.
Not tested: no robustness claim against attacks.

record.verdict_notes: The target knowledge was first inserted by continual pretraining (θpre), and unlearning is measured against that model. Ablation values were reconstructed from the flattened Table 1, and they match the prose (10% higher unlearn and 8% lower retain for θgd; no unlearn drop for θgd+kl). The ablations are component analyses of the study's own method, so they are unlinked from version A. Only one model is tested, with no uncertainty reported. The paper is a preprint.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not test whether simple attacks recover the knowledge. The reported unlearn accuracy is a reduction, but the paper does not state a chance level.
No post-unlearning recovery fine-tuning on unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten-fact examples.
No activation-direction ablation or test distinguishing blocked access from deletion.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, other-language, or in-context recovery tests.
No test of a method resisting the recovery attacks.

rows.subject: θsurgery
rows.stage_stated: Continually pretrained as θpre, then modified with LLM Surgery
rows.operation_detail: LLM Surgery: gradient ascent on unlearn data, gradient descent on update data, and KL-divergence minimization on retain data
rows.note: The paper describes this as a 19% reduction from θpre and also says it is 4% lower than off-the-shelf Llama2-7B. No chance-level value is stated.
rows.check: A chance level can be derived. The benchmark has three answer choices (Section 3.1), so chance is about 33.3%. The value of 41.86 is well above chance and only 4 points below off-the-shelf Llama2-7B (45.81). The state partial is correct; the note that no chance level is stated should be corrected.

rows.subject: θsurgery

rows.operation_detail: LLM Surgery: gradient ascent on unlearn data, gradient descent on update data, and KL-divergence minimization on retain data
rows.note: The authors describe performance on ARC-Easy as comparable to θpre.
rows.check: ARC-Easy falls from 56.93 to 51.94, about 5 points, and is about 9 points below off-the-shelf Llama2-7B (60.81). The authors call this comparable, but the drop is noticeable, so partial is a better state than observed.

rows.subject: θgd
rows.stage_stated: Ablation of LLM Surgery, starting from θpre
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent on the update dataset only; gradient-ascent and KL-divergence terms omitted
rows.value: 10% higher accuracy than θsurgery; exact value not stated in the accompanying text
rows.note: The authors say this ablation has insufficient unlearning. The flattened table does not support assigning its unlearn value unambiguously.
rows.check: This is an ablation of the study's own method with no unlearning term, not an unlearning method under version A. The flattened table can be read consistently with the prose: θgd unlearn 51.23 (about 10 points above 41.86), update 66.78, retain 55.31, ARC 54.65. The value should be 51.23.

relationships.condition: LLM Surgery on continually pretrained Llama2-7B, 3-choice MCQA unlearn benchmark
relationships.reason: Unlearn accuracy drops from 60.86 to 41.86, still well above 33.3% chance and near off-the-shelf 45.81 (R1). Retain accuracy is roughly kept (63.02 to 60.4, R2), but ARC-Easy falls about 5 points (R3).
relationships.display_finding: Unlearn accuracy fell from 60.86 to 41.86 against 33.3% chance and an off-the-shelf score of 45.81, while retain accuracy changed from 63.02 to 60.4 and ARC-Easy fell about 5 points.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Unlearn accuracy decreases from 60.86 to 41.86 but the paper does not report a chance-level comparison; retain and ARC-Easy performance are described as comparable (R1–R3). Recovery attacks are not tested.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The gradient-descent-only ablation has insufficient unlearning and reduced retain performance, while the gradient-descent-plus-KL ablation does not unlearn the target (R4–R7).
